slides.title: Every number you show this week can be traced to its definition and its rows
slides.text: How this course works Every number you show this week can be traced to its definition and its rows Reproduce first Before you argue about a number, compute it again from its written rule. Define once One name, one formula, one owner. A second meaning gets a second name. Test it Hand-computed values, source totals and reference queries, every day. AI policy. AI off for the first lab of each day and for the supervised check. A tutor in the other labs, explaining errors without writing your definitions. In the capstone an assistant may draft; every drafted definition carries a verification note. On Day 4 the agent is under test, not your helper.

slides.title: Wadi Noor Transit: twelve bus routes, three depots, three on-time figures
slides.text: One case study all week Wadi Noor Transit: twelve bus routes, three depots, three on-time figures A fictional city bus operator (نقل وادي نور). Synthetic data from January to October 2026. You are the new performance reporting analyst. Mashael Al-Saadi Operations director. Decides every Sunday where the reserve buses and supervisors go. Three report owners Tawfiq Al-Sahafi (control centre), Dhuha Al-Rowais (planning), Yasmeen Al-Jaafari (board pack). Muneer and Haneen Muneer Al-Thaqafi owns the warehouse; Haneen Al-Shamrani owns data classification.

slides.text: Session 1 Why three reports disagree Name the four places two definitions of one measure can differ Reproduce a published figure from its written rule Explain a gap between two figures one rule at a time 01

slides.title: One warehouse, one month, three on-time figures
slides.text: The problem you inherit One warehouse, one month, three on-time figures 80.7% Operations report, September 66.0% Planning service review, September 58.4% Board pack, September meeting Nobody made an arithmetic error. Each figure is right for its own rule.

slides.title: The three owners wrote three different rules under one name
slides.text: Read the rules, not the totals The three owners wrote three different rules under one name Report Counts On time means Cancelled trips Period Operations (Tawfiq) trips left the first stop 1 min early to 5 late left out September Planning (Dhuha) timepoint arrivals 1 min early to 5 late, at every timepoint no arrivals to count September Board (Yasmeen) trips reached the terminus at most 5 min late count as late Rabi al-Thani 1448 Source: labs/data/reports/three_reports.yaml, the sentence under each report.

slides.title: Two definitions of one measure differ in four places
slides.text: Where definitions differ Two definitions of one measure differ in four places Grain What is counted: trips, timepoint arrivals, riders, cards. Rule Where it is measured and the tolerance: first stop or terminus, early allowed or not. Filter What enters the denominator: cancelled trips, partial trips, holidays. Period Which dates: Gregorian month, Hijri month, a Sunday week or an ISO week. Use it as a checklist. Two figures that disagree differ in at least one of these four. Find which before you look for a bug.

slides.title: Change one rule at a time and the gap explains itself
slides.text: A reconciliation walk Change one rule at a time and the gap explains itself Operations rules 80.7% Measured at the terminus 50.4% Early arrivals allowed 59.7% Cancelled trips count as late 58.0% Hijri month, not September 58.4%

slides.title: Counting timepoints, not trips, asks a different question
slides.text: The biggest step Counting timepoints, not trips, asks a different question Per trip, at the first stop "Did the bus leave when the timetable said?" The rider waiting at the start can plan on it. Per timepoint arrival "Was the bus on time along the way?" Delays build up, so later timepoints pull the figure down. Neither is wrong. Planning's 66.0% is the honest answer to its own question. The fault is the shared name.

slides.title: A disputed number spends the meeting on the number, not the decision
slides.text: Why it matters A disputed number spends the meeting on the number, not the decision Three figures invite each team to quote the one that suits it Every new report adds a definition nobody wrote down An agent asked "what was on-time performance?" will pick one, and not say which The fix is not a fourth report: it is one catalogue, one owner per metric

slides.text: Checkpoint Why is the planning figure lower? Planning reads a stale copy of the data Planning counts every timepoint arrival, where delays have built up Planning counts cancelled trips as late Planning reports a Hijri month

slides.title: Anatomy of a metric definition
slides.text: Session 2 Anatomy of a metric definition Write a definition with formula, grain, filters, time logic, owner and limits Tell taps, cards and journeys apart Reconcile a definition to the source totals 02

slides.title: "Ridership last week" is four different numbers
slides.text: One word, four numbers "Ridership last week" is four different numbers Card taps 19,826 Linked journeys 16,231 Card-days 13,992 Different cards 9,864 The week of 13 to 19 September 2026, from Lab 1.2.

slides.title: A tap, a journey and a card count different things
slides.text: Counting units in transit A tap, a journey and a card count different things Tap one card at one validator, every boarding → Journey taps of one card within 60 minutes linked as one trip → Card-day one card that travelled on a day → Card one card seen in the period The trap. Each step to the right is distinct within its period, so it is no longer additive: card-days add across days, cards do not.

slides.title: A definition someone else can compute has eight parts
slides.text: Anatomy of a definition A definition someone else can compute has eight parts Name and the question it answers Formula : one aggregate, or a ratio of two Grain : what one counted row is Filters : what is in and out Time logic : which date, which calendar, which week Unit of the result Owner : a person and their role Limits : what it must not be used for The test. Give it to a colleague: if they compute your number without asking you anything, it is a definition.

slides.title: The journeys definition, as the catalogue holds it
slides.text: An entry of the catalogue The journeys definition, as the catalogue holds it - name: journeys question: How many journeys did riders make, counting a transfer as part of one journey? formula: SUM(journey_start) table: boarding_linked grain: one card tap, journey_start = 1 when the card made no tap in the 60 minutes before filters: none time_logic: service_date of the tap; the 60-minute look-back crosses midnight unit: journeys owner: Dhuha Al-Rowais, network planning manager limits: a return trip within 60 minutes counts as a transfer

slides.title: An owner decides what the metric means; a change gets a new version
slides.text: Owners and change control An owner decides what the metric means; a change gets a new version The owner answers questions about the definition and approves changes A change that moves the number is announced, dated and versioned A second meaning is a second metric with its own name and owner The board's measure stays, renamed terminal_on_time_rate, owned by Yasmeen

slides.title: A definition reconciles when its formula, run as written, gives the source total
slides.text: Proof, not belief A definition reconciles when its formula, run as written, gives the source total for d in defs: got = W.measure(con, d, *WEEK) W.check(got == counts[d["name"]], d["name"]) Run the formula on the table the definition names, for the period Compare with the count taken directly from the source Add a sum test: taps by route plus taps without a route equal all taps

slides.title: The dictionary marks what a metric may count but never show
slides.text: Responsible use, from the first definition The dictionary marks what a metric may count but never show card_id is pseudonymous personal data: Restricted Counting distinct cards is allowed; listing them is not The PDPL limits personal data to the minimum the purpose needs Counts of cards are not shown below 10 Four levels The NDMO Data Classification Policy has four: Top Secret, Secret, Restricted, Public. Label every field the catalogue uses.

slides.title: Ratios, distinct counts and time logic
slides.text: Session 3 Ratios, distinct counts and time logic Compute a ratio of sums and say why it differs from a mean of ratios Explain why distinct counts do not add across periods Test a metric against hand-computed values 03

slides.title: A network rate is a ratio of sums, not a mean of route rates
slides.text: Ratios A network rate is a ratio of sums, not a mean of route rates Route Departed On time Rate A 100 90 90% B 10 5 50% C 40 30 75% Network 150 125 83.3% 71.7% mean of the three route rates Not the network The mean gives route B's ten trips the weight of route A's hundred.

slides.title: A mean of ratios answers "how does a typical route do?"
slides.text: When the mean is right A mean of ratios answers "how does a typical route do?" Network performance: ratio of sums, each trip counted once The typical route: mean of route ratios, each route counted once Both are legitimate; they are two metrics with two names A dashboard that averages a column of percentages has chosen the second without saying so

slides.title: Weekly distinct cards do not add up to a month
slides.text: Distinct counts Weekly distinct cards do not add up to a month Week starting Distinct cards 2026-09-06 9,909 2026-09-13 9,864 2026-09-20 9,257 2026-09-27 9,734 38,764 the four weeks added 22,962 distinct over the four weeks

slides.title: Flows add over time; snapshots do not
slides.text: Flows and snapshots Flows add over time; snapshots do not Flow Taps, trips, complaints: events in a period. A month is the sum of its days. Snapshot Active passes, buses in service, open complaints: a state on a date. A month is a chosen day, or an average of days, never a sum. State the rule. A snapshot metric's time logic names the day it is taken: the last day of the period, or the mean of daily values.

slides.title: Which date, which week, which calendar
slides.text: Time logic Which date, which week, which calendar Choice At Wadi Noor What goes wrong otherwise The date that places a row the service date of the trip a trip after midnight lands on the next day The week Sunday to Saturday ISO weeks start on Monday and split the working week The month Gregorian unless a Hijri month is named Ramadan and the Eids move eleven days a year Like with like compare holiday timetables with holidays National Day looks like a fall in demand

slides.title: Test a metric on an example you computed by hand, then on the source
slides.text: Testing a metric Test a metric on an example you computed by hand, then on the source 1 · By hand a toy of three routes, with fractions on paper → 2 · Same rows the toy as a table the function can read → 3 · Equal the function returns the hand value exactly → 4 · Network the function on September, against a reference Also test what it must not equal. The toy's ratio of sums must differ from its mean of ratios: a test that would pass with the wrong formula proves nothing.

slides.title: Metric trees
slides.text: Session 4 Metric trees Decompose a goal metric into drivers that multiply back to it Add a guardrail that a driver could harm Assign an owner to each node 04

slides.title: A metric tree links one goal to the drivers that teams can move
slides.text: Metric trees A metric tree links one goal to the drivers that teams can move Goal weekly card taps = Timetable scheduled trips × Delivery 1 − cancellation rate × Demand taps per departed trip Guardrail. Complaints per 10,000 taps: it watches for harm a driver could do, such as crowding more riders onto each bus.

slides.title: Multiply for rates and volumes, add for segments
slides.text: Two kinds of tree Multiply for rates and volumes, add for segments Multiplicative Taps = trips × (1 − cancelled) × taps per trip. Changes combine as products; log changes add. Additive Taps = North + Central + East. Each segment's change adds to the total; Day 3 drills down this way. Use both. Multiply to find which driver moved; add to find where it moved.

slides.title: Taps fell 8.5%: the timetable explains almost all of it
slides.text: The tree on two weeks Taps fell 8.5%: the timetable explains almost all of it Node Week of 13 Sep Week of 20 Sep Change Taps (goal) 19,826 18,146 -8.5% Scheduled trips 1,950 1,794 -8.0% 1 − cancellation rate 97.0% 97.7% +0.8% Taps per departed trip 10.48 10.35 -1.3%

slides.title: Every node has an owner, and the guardrail has a direction
slides.text: Owners on the nodes Every node has an owner, and the guardrail has a direction Node Owner Taps Muneer Al-Thaqafi, data platform Scheduled trips, taps per departed trip Dhuha Al-Rowais, planning Cancellation rate Tawfiq Al-Sahafi, control centre Complaints per 10,000 taps (guardrail, worry if up) Yasmeen Al-Jaafari, strategy

slides.title: A tree misleads when its drivers overlap or do not reconcile
slides.text: What goes wrong A tree misleads when its drivers overlap or do not reconcile Two drivers that count the same thing double its effect A driver measured at another grain or period breaks the product A driver nobody owns is a number nobody acts on A tree with no guardrail rewards crowding, skipping stops or cutting short trips

slides.title: The NDMO standards ask for analytics KPIs, measured and registered
slides.text: The national standard The NDMO standards ask for analytics KPIs, measured and registered The Business Intelligence and Analytics domain has 5 controls and 10 specifications It asks for a plan, prioritised use cases, validation of their outcomes, KPIs and a register A governed catalogue is the register of what each number means For this course Each dashboard is a use case: validate it, and record the metrics it shows with their owners.

slides.title: Which driver belongs in the tree?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which driver belongs in the tree? The tree is taps = scheduled trips × (1 − cancellation rate) × taps per departed trip. A colleague proposes adding "on-time rate" as a fourth driver. What do you say? Add it: punctuality drives demand Replace the cancellation rate with it Keep it beside the tree, as a guardrail or its own goal Leave it out of the review

slides.title: A definition says what a number means; a model computes it the same way everywhere
slides.text: From catalogue to model A definition says what a number means; a model computes it the same way everywhere Catalogue meaning, owner, limits (Day 1) → Star schema facts at a grain, dimensions to slice by → Semantic model each metric written once, joins decided once → Every consumer dashboard, notebook, agent

slides.title: Facts record events at a grain; dimensions describe them
slides.text: Two kinds of table Facts record events at a grain; dimensions describe them Facts Trips, timepoint arrivals, taps, complaints. Many rows, numeric columns to aggregate, foreign keys to dimensions. Dimensions Routes, dates, vehicles, depots. Few rows, descriptive columns to group and filter by, one key each. Ask of every column: do I add it up, or do I slice by it? The answer places it in a fact or in a dimension.

slides.title: Four facts share dates, routes and vehicles
slides.text: The star Four facts share dates, routes and vehicles fct_trip fct_boarding fct_timepoint fct_complaint dim_route dim_date dim_vehicle Facts are rectangles, dimensions rounded. Every line is many-to-one, from the fact to what it points at.

slides.title: A grain is a sentence; a key test proves it
slides.text: Recap from FN-104 A grain is a sentence; a key test proves it SELECT count(*) AS rows, count(DISTINCT (trip_id, tp_seq)) AS keys, count(*) FILTER (WHERE trip_id IS NULL OR tp_seq IS NULL) AS empty FROM fct_timepoint; fct_timepoint: one departed trip at one timepoint 329,188 rows, 329,188 keys, none empty: the grain holds Grain, keys and orphans were taught in FN-104, Day 1; today they are the input of a model

slides.title: dim_route has 13 rows for 12 routes
slides.text: The planted surprise dim_route has 13 rows for 12 routes route_key route_id route_name_en length_km valid_from valid_to 7 R07 Al-Rawdah Feeder 11.4 2026-01-01 2026-05-31 8 R07 Al-Rawdah Hospital Feeder 15.8 2026-06-01 (open) route_id is the natural key riders use; route_key identifies one version A join on route_id returns 91,418 rows for 85,010 trips: every R07 trip twice

slides.title: When a route changes, decide whether history changes with it
slides.text: Slowly changing dimensions When a route changes, decide whether history changes with it Type 1: overwrite The new value replaces the old everywhere, past included. Right for corrections: a misspelt name. Type 2: add a version A new row with its own key and validity dates. Right for real changes: a longer route, a new depot. The test. Would a January figure be wrong if it used the June value? Then it is type 2.

slides.title: Join each fact row to the version valid on its date
slides.text: The as-of join Join each fact row to the version valid on its date SELECT t.*, r.route_key, r.route_name_en, r.length_km FROM fct_trip t JOIN dim_route r ON r.route_id = t.route_id AND t.service_date >= r.valid_from AND (r.valid_to IS NULL OR t.service_date <= r.valid_to) 85,010 trips in, 85,010 rows out. The open valid_to means "still valid".

slides.title: Fan-out and join paths
slides.text: Session 3 Fan-out and join paths Recognise a join that repeats rows Write a reconciliation test against a source total Aggregate each fact before joining 03

slides.title: Yasmeen's route report counts 334,786 taps in a month of 84,063
slides.text: A report that adds up wrong Yasmeen's route report counts 334,786 taps in a month of 84,063 SELECT t.route_id, count(b.tap_id) AS taps, avg(CASE WHEN p.delay_min BETWEEN -1 AND 5 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) FROM fct_trip t JOIN fct_boarding b ON b.trip_id = t.trip_id JOIN fct_timepoint p ON p.trip_id = t.trip_id WHERE t.service_date BETWEEN ... GROUP BY t.route_id

slides.title: Joining two "many" sides through one row multiplies both
slides.text: The fan trap Joining two "many" sides through one row multiplies both 8,268 trips September → 84,063 rows each trip once per tap → 334,786 rows each tap once per timepoint 3.98 times. Every tap is repeated by the number of timepoints its trip reached: four, or two for a partial trip.

slides.title: The punctuality column is wrong too, and nothing looks odd
slides.text: The quieter error The punctuality column is wrong too, and nothing looks odd 49.0% R01 timepoint punctuality in the report 51.1% R01 timepoint punctuality, computed alone After the join each arrival is weighted by the taps of its trip: busy, late trips count more.

slides.title: A reconciliation test compares the report with the source counted another way
slides.text: The test that catches it A reconciliation test compares the report with the source counted another way def reconciles(df) -> bool: source = W.scalar(con, """SELECT count(*) FROM fct_boarding WHERE service_date BETWEEN ... AND trip_id IS NOT NULL""") return int(df.taps.sum()) == int(source) Write it first and watch it fail on the faulty report Then fix the query, and watch it pass

slides.title: Aggregate each fact to the shared grain, then join
slides.text: The fix Aggregate each fact to the shared grain, then join WITH taps AS (SELECT t.route_id, count(*) AS taps FROM fct_boarding b JOIN fct_trip t USING (trip_id) ... GROUP BY 1), punct AS (SELECT t.route_id, avg(...) AS timepoint_on_time FROM fct_timepoint p JOIN fct_trip t USING (trip_id) ... GROUP BY 1) SELECT route_id, taps, timepoint_on_time FROM taps JOIN punct USING (route_id) Each fact joins only "up" to trips, which is many-to-one; the two results meet at one row per route.

slides.title: A semantic model joins only towards the "one" side
slides.text: The rule a model enforces A semantic model joins only towards the "one" side Every relationship is declared from the many side to the one side A metric is aggregated in its own dataset, joining only along those arrows A grouping that needs a "many" side is refused, not computed Two metrics of two facts are aggregated apart, then joined on the dimensions asked for request boardings by timepoints.tp_seq refused no many-to-one path from boardings to timepoints: grouping would repeat rows

slides.title: Where does the report go wrong?
slides.text: Checkpoint Where does the report go wrong? A report joins complaints and taps to routes in one query and counts both per route. Complaints come out about 7,000 times too high. What happened? The complaints table has duplicate rows Each complaint was repeated once per tap of its route: two facts met through one dimension The date filter was left out The join should have been a left join

slides.title: The double-counting join
slides.text: Lab 2.3 · 25 min The double-counting join Find the join that inflates boardings in a route report, write a reconciliation test that fails on it, and fix the query by aggregating before joining. D2_3_fan_out.ipynb Run the route report as written 5 min Find the join that repeats rows 6 min Write a reconciliation test that fails on it 6 min Fix the query by aggregating before joining 8 min ✱ Stretch: Ask the semantic layer for the same report and read its refusal

slides.title: Metrics in an open specification
slides.text: Session 4 Metrics in an open specification Write datasets, fields, relationships and metrics in an Apache Ossie document Tell a dataset-scoped from a model-scoped metric Validate a model and run test queries against it 04

slides.title: Write each metric once; every tool asks for it by name
slides.text: The point of a semantic layer Write each metric once; every tool asks for it by name Without it Each dashboard, notebook and agent writes its own SQL for "on-time rate". Three teams, three queries, three numbers. With it The model holds datasets, joins and metrics. A tool asks for on_time_rate by route type; the layer writes the SQL. MetricFlowCube CoreApache Ossie files

slides.title: Apache Ossie is a vendor-neutral file format for semantic models
slides.text: An open specification Apache Ossie is a vendor-neutral file format for semantic models Formerly Open Semantic Interchange (OSI); renamed on entering the Apache Incubator in 2026 One YAML or JSON document per model: datasets, fields, relationships, metrics A JSON Schema checks the document; converters move it between tools The version in this course, 0.3.0.dev0, is still in development: re-check before each cohort

slides.title: Datasets with fields, relationships from many to one, metrics
slides.text: What the file holds Datasets with fields, relationships from many to one, metrics datasets: - name: trips source: SELECT t.*, r.route_key FROM fct_trip t LEFT JOIN dim_route r ON ... primary_key: [trip_id] fields: - {name: status, expression: {sql: status}, dimension: {}} metrics: - name: departed_trips expression: {sql: "SUM(CASE WHEN status <> 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)"} relationships: - {name: trips_to_routes, from: trips, to: routes, from_columns: [route_key], to_columns: [route_key]}

slides.title: Dataset metrics aggregate one dataset; model metrics combine them
slides.text: Two places for a metric Dataset metrics aggregate one dataset; model metrics combine them Dataset-scoped boardings.unique_cards: COUNT(DISTINCT card_id), bare field names of its own dataset. Model-scoped on_time_rate: AGG(trips.on_time_departures) / AGG(trips.departed_trips), each part aggregated first. AGG() is the ratio of sums. The division happens after both parts are aggregated, so the layer cannot average ratios by mistake.

slides.title: One request, compiled to the SQL of Session 3
slides.text: What the layer generates One request, compiled to the SQL of Session 3 request on_time_rate by routes.route_type, where dates.gregorian_month = '2026-09' datasets one common table expression each for trips, routes, dates aggregate trips joined to routes and dates (many-to-one), summed by route type divide on_time_departures / departed_trips: express 89.3%, feeder 82.8%, trunk 67.0%

slides.title: Access rules ride in an extension that other tools may ignore
slides.text: What the interchange does not carry Access rules ride in an extension that other tools may ignore nonportable_extensions: - vendor_name: WADI_NOOR data: roles: network_analyst: {clearance: Public} east_depot_manager: clearance: Public row_filter: "routes.depot = 'East'" Fields carry a classification: card_id and complaint_text are Restricted A role may count a Restricted field, never group, filter or show it Ossie defines no access rules: every consumer must enforce them again

slides.title: 25 test queries, each with a reference computed without the model
slides.text: Proving the model 25 test queries, each with a reference computed without the model Each test is a request (metrics, dimensions, filters) and its expected rows The expected rows come from independent SQL, written by hand, not from the layer They cover ratios, distinct counts, Hijri months, the R07 versions, holidays and the October week 25 of 25 is the evidence for the third course outcome

slides.title: Where does the cancellation rate go?
slides.text: Checkpoint Where does the cancellation rate go? You add cancellation_rate to the model. The trips dataset already has cancelled_trips and scheduled_trips. What do you write? A dataset metric AVG(status = 'cancelled') on trips, used by every ratio A SQL snippet in each dashboard that needs it A model metric that averages a daily cancellation rate A model metric AGG(trips.cancelled_trips) / AGG(trips.scheduled_trips)

slides.text: Day 2 · wrap-up Three things to keep Grain and history Prove each grain; join a fact to the dimension version valid on its date. Aggregate, then join Count rows after each join; reconcile totals; never join two "many" sides. Define once One open document holds datasets, joins and metrics; 25 tests prove it.

slides.title: A dashboard serves one audience making one decision on a cadence
slides.text: What a dashboard is for A dashboard serves one audience making one decision on a cadence Audience Mashael Al-Saadi, operations director, and the three depot managers; two read Arabic first. Decision Where the six reserve buses and four field supervisors go next week. Cadence Sunday morning, before the depots open; data to Saturday. What goes wrong. "A dashboard for operations" names no decision, so every question qualifies and the page fills up.

slides.title: Nine good questions; four of them decide
slides.text: The brief Nine good questions; four of them decide Question Serves the decision? Q1 Which routes leave late, against the 85% target? decides Q2 Where were trips cancelled? decides Q3 Which routes are crowded? decides Q4 What are riders complaining about? decides Q5 Network taps this week context Q6 Revenue by product · Q7 Top card numbers · Q8 Next month's forecast no Q9 Delay by timepoint on one route drill-through

slides.title: A panel is a question, a governed metric, a split, a comparison and an owner
slides.text: From question to panel A panel is a question, a governed metric, a split, a comparison and an owner - title: Routes leaving late question: Q1 metric: on_time_rate # from the semantic model dimensions: [routes.route_id] comparison: target # 85%, from the brief also: the route's level over the four weeks before owner: Tawfiq Al-Sahafi, control centre Only governed metrics. A panel that cannot name a metric of the model is asking for a definition first.

slides.title: A number alone does not say whether to act
slides.text: Comparisons A number alone does not say whether to act Target 76% against 85%: below the promise. Prior period 76% against a usual 86%: a bad week. Peer 76% against other feeders at 77% to 90%: this route. Pick the comparison the decision needs. A reserve bus fixes a bad week, so Q1 shows the target and the usual level.

slides.title: The wish list gets 13 findings; five panels get none
slides.text: The brief checker The wish list gets 13 findings; five panels get none 9 panels: a decision dashboard has at most six Q6, Q7, Q8 do not serve the decision fare_revenue and ridership_forecast are not metrics of the model boardings.card_id is Restricted and cannot be shown Six panels have no comparison The wireframe Late routes, cancellations by depot, riders per trip, complaints by subject, network taps; Q9 as a drill-through.

slides.title: A dashboard is an analytics use case: plan it, validate it, register it
slides.text: The national standard A dashboard is an analytics use case: plan it, validate it, register it The NDMO Business Intelligence and Analytics domain asks for identified, prioritised use cases It asks that their outcomes be validated, personal data protection included The wireframe is the use case; the brief checker and Lab 3.3's equality test are the validation

Revenue by fare product this month On-time departures by route against the target Taps per departed trip by route Cancellation rate by depot against last week

slides.text: Session 2 Comparisons and bilingual layout Show a number against a target and a prior period Lay out the same panel in Arabic and English Suppress small counts before publishing 02

slides.title: Every panel asks the semantic layer, never the raw tables
slides.text: From wireframe to panels Every panel asks the semantic layer, never the raw tables w = ["dates.week_start = DATE '2026-10-25'"] model.query(["on_time_rate", "trips.departed_trips"], ["routes.route_id", "routes.route_name_en", "routes.route_name_ar"], w) The same definition as the catalogue and the 25 tests Arabic and English route names come from the model, not from a translation table in the chart

slides.title: Eight routes miss 85%; only some of them had a bad week
slides.text: The week of 25 October Eight routes miss 85%; only some of them had a bad week Route Last week Usual (4 weeks) Reading R09 East Trunk 60.8% 65.7% always far below: timetable R01 Al-Nakheel to City Centre 66.4% 69.6% always below: timetable R11 Al-Faisaliyah Feeder 76.4% 85.5% a bad week: reserve bus R02 Al-Wurud Loop 77.7% 85.2% a bad week: reserve bus Two comparisons, two actions. The target says "below"; the usual level says "unusual".

slides.title: In Arabic the panel mirrors; it is not only translated
slides.text: Two directions In Arabic the panel mirrors; it is not only translated English, left to right Labels on the left; bars grow to the right; the title starts on the left. Arabic, right to left Labels on the right; bars grow to the left; the title starts on the right; the page has dir="rtl". Digits stay Western (0 to 9) in both, as in the Academy's Arabic material Route names from route_name_ar; subjects from a reviewed list, never machine-translated on the fly

slides.title: Counts below ten are hidden, and the page says so
slides.text: Before publishing Counts below ten are hidden, and the page says so Complaints by subject, one week: 4 of 6 subjects have fewer than 10 Small counts can point to a person and move by chance The threshold is in the model's extension: small_count_threshold: 10 Hidden values are removed from the data, not only from the chart On the page "fewer than 10: accessibility, card, cleanliness, driver". The subject is named; its count is not.

slides.title: Meaning must survive without colour
slides.text: Colour Meaning must survive without colour Pair Contrast teal bar on white 5.47 to 1 orange tick on white 5.18 to 1 teal bar against orange tick 1.06 to 1 A different mark, not only a different colour. The usual level is a tick and the target a dashed rule, so they read apart even where the two colours do not.

slides.text: Checkpoint What does the Arabic panel need? The English crowding panel is finished. A colleague makes the Arabic one by translating the title and the axis label. What is still wrong? The digits must become Eastern Arabic The numbers must be recomputed for Arabic readers The colours must change The route labels and the start of the bars must move to the right, with Arabic route names

slides.title: Load time is a design constraint
slides.text: Session 3 Load time is a design constraint Measure a dashboard tile by tile Replace per-tile queries with one grouped query Pre-aggregate to the grain the panels need, keeping the parts of each ratio 03

slides.title: Three seconds is part of the brief, like the decision
slides.text: The budget Three seconds is part of the brief, like the decision Mashael opens the page on a tablet at the depot; a slow page is not opened twice The budget is measured, not felt: time each part, then add The work splits into refresh time (night) and view time (Sunday morning) Only view time counts against the budget

slides.title: One query per tile: 672 queries, 24.6 seconds
slides.text: Where the seconds go One query per tile: 672 queries, 24.6 seconds for r in ROUTES: # 12 for d in days: # 28 model.value("on_time_rate", [r, d]) model.value("boardings_per_departed_trip", [r, d]) Each query reads the files, plans the joins and returns one number The work is the same; only the filter changes The pattern has a name: N+1 queries

slides.title: One grouped query at refresh time, one small read at view time
slides.text: Step by step One grouped query at refresh time, one small read at view time 1 · Group once route by day, from the semantic layer → 2 · Keep the parts on-time departures, departed trips, taps → 3 · Read the table every tile in one query: 0.005 s Takeaway. The table took 0.04 s to build; the dashboard became thousands of times faster.

slides.title: Store the numerator and the denominator, never the rate
slides.text: Ratios in an aggregate table Store the numerator and the denominator, never the rate A week's rate is the sum of on-time departures over the sum of departed trips The mean of seven daily rates gives Friday, with half the trips, a full vote Week of 25 October: the mean of daily rates is off by up to 1.9 points on a route Day 1, again The ratio of sums from Lab 1.3, now as a rule for any table that feeds a dashboard.

slides.title: A faster dashboard that shows other numbers is a new dashboard
slides.text: The equality test A faster dashboard that shows other numbers is a new dashboard Compare every tile, slow against fast, before switching In the first run, 16 crowding tiles differed: 0 in the slow version, empty in the fast one Those route-days had no tap with a route (East, 5 to 8 October): the table must hold 0, not nothing State freshness under the title: "Data to 31 October"

slides.title: What goes in the route-day table?
slides.text: Checkpoint What goes in the route-day table? The dashboard shows on-time rate by route for any week and depot. You pre-aggregate to one row per route and day. Which columns do you store? The daily on-time rate Every trip with its delay On-time departures and departed trips The weekly on-time rate, repeated on each day

D3_3_load_time.ipynb Time the tile-by-tile dashboard 5 min Build a route-day table with the parts of each ratio 8 min Redraw the dashboard from the table and time it 7 min Prove the numbers did not change, and date the data 5 min ✱ Stretch: Refresh only the newest day

slides.title: Investigating an anomaly
slides.text: Session 4 Investigating an anomaly Drill a change down a tree of segments Tell a data fault from a change in demand Write an anomaly note with cause, segments and correction 04

slides.title: "Route ridership down 17% in the week of 4 October"
slides.text: Monday's network pack "Route ridership down 17% in the week of 4 October" Route taps: 16,210 against 19,615 the week before The board asks which routes lost their riders Planning drafts a timetable cut for the East First question Not "who left?" but "is the drop in the riders or in the data?"

slides.title: All taps rose 2.5%; taps with a route fell 17.4%
slides.text: Confirm the drop All taps rose 2.5%; taps with a route fell 17.4% Week of All taps Taps with a route 2026-09-27 19,615 19,615 2026-10-04 20,112 16,210 2026-10-11 19,863 19,863 3,902 taps are in the data and missing from the pack: they lost their route, not their riders.

slides.title: Follow the gap down until it has an address
slides.text: Drill down Follow the gap down until it has an address Network -3,405 route taps → Depot East: 5,533 to 1,862 → Bus depot East buses: 5,533 to 5,764 → Day no route on 5 to 8 October Takeaway. By route the East lost two thirds; by bus it gained. The buses kept their riders.

slides.title: A fault hits everyone alike; a change in demand does not
slides.text: Segment A fault hits everyone alike; a change in demand does not Demand Students fall on a school holiday; adults fall in a heatwave; segments move unevenly. Data On 5 to 8 October, 100% of taps on East buses lost their route, for every fare type alike. The cause. dim_vehicle shows the East validators updated from firmware 2.4 to 3.0 on 5 October.

slides.title: Restated by bus, the week of 4 October is ordinary
slides.text: Correct Restated by bus, the week of 4 October is ordinary Each tap kept its bus; each bus has a home route; an as-of join finds the trip Validated first: on 1 to 3 October the as-of join finds the recorded trip for 100% of R09's taps Restated route taps: 20,112, +2.5% on the week before No route lost riders; the timetable cut is withdrawn

slides.title: Four lines: seen, cause, size, change
slides.text: The anomaly note Four lines: seen, cause, size, change seen route taps -17% in the week of 4 October (16,210 against 19,615) cause East validator update of 5 October: 3,902 taps without route or trip to 8 October size restated by bus, 20,112 taps (+2.5%); no route lost riders change the pack shows taps without a route; a test fails above 1% a day

slides.title: The network improved while every route type got worse
slides.text: When the mix moves The network improved while every route type got worse On time August September Departed trips, Aug to Sep express 92.3% 89.3% 873 to 1,864 feeder 83.0% 82.8% 4,498 to 4,312 trunk 69.6% 67.0% 3,210 to 1,857 network 79.0% 80.7%

slides.title: Data or demand?
slides.text: Checkpoint Data or demand? Route taps on the East depot fell by two thirds for four days. Taps on East buses did not fall. Every fare type lost its route in the same share. What do you conclude? East riders moved to other routes A recording fault: the taps lost their route, not their riders A school holiday in the East East trips were cancelled

slides.title: From question to query
slides.text: Session 1 From question to query Describe the steps from a question to a query Log every query an agent runs Judge an answer against a governed figure 01

slides.title: Nabih turns a question into a query, runs it, and answers
slides.text: The agent Nabih turns a question into a query, runs it, and answers 1 · Question a depot manager writes in the chat → 2 · Query a language model writes SQL or a metric request → 3 · Run the query runs on the warehouse → 4 · Answer a number in a sentence Takeaway. Only step 2 is generated; steps 3 and 4 can be logged and checked.

slides.title: Text-to-SQL that looks solved on benchmarks drops on real schemas
slides.text: What benchmarks say Text-to-SQL that looks solved on benchmarks drops on real schemas Benchmark Best reported accuracy Spider 1.0 (small, clean schemas) 91.2% BIRD (larger, dirtier databases) 73.0% Spider 2.0 (enterprise workflows) 21.3% What goes wrong. A benchmark score is not your score. Your schema, your definitions and your questions decide it.

slides.title: Given only tables and columns, the agent guesses the definitions
slides.text: The raw configuration Given only tables and columns, the agent guesses the definitions fct_trip(trip_id BIGINT, service_date DATE, route_id VARCHAR, status VARCHAR, dep_delay_min DOUBLE, arr_delay_min DOUBLE, ...) fct_complaint(..., complaint_text VARCHAR) Reply with JSON only: {"sql": "..."} Nothing says on time is measured at departure Nothing says weeks start on Sunday Nothing says complaint_text is Restricted

slides.title: Three of ten right, and every query ran without an error
slides.text: Lab 4.1, in advance Three of ten right, and every query ran without an error Question What the SQL did Error Complaints, week of 4 October Monday to Sunday period Network on time, September arrival at the terminus: 60.7% definition Trunk on time, September mean of daily rates: 67.1% against 67.0% grain Complaints per 10,000 taps joined complaints to taps: 5,394 join Text of driver complaints returned the text leak

slides.title: Log the query, the mode and the model of every answer
slides.text: Watching the agent Log the query, the mode and the model of every answer {"id": "Q09", "config": "raw", "mode": "stand-in", "query": "SELECT avg((arr_delay_min <= 5)::INT) FROM fct_trip ...", "value": 0.6066, "refused": false, "seconds": 0.02} The query is the only evidence of which definition the agent used The mode says whether a model or the scripted stand-in wrote it

slides.title: Is this answer right?
slides.text: Checkpoint Is this answer right? Nabih answers "80.4% of trips were on time in September". Its SQL ran without an error. The certified figure is 80.7% with a tolerance of 0.1 points. What do you mark? Right: the query ran Right: it is close enough Wrong: it is outside the tolerance; read the query to find why Update the certified figure

D4_1_agent_raw.ipynb Read the schema the agent is given 4 min Run the agent on ten questions and log its SQL 8 min Mark each answer against the governed figure 8 min Name what went wrong in each wrong answer 5 min ✱ Stretch: Change one line of the instruction and run again

slides.title: Certified questions
slides.text: Session 2 Certified questions Write a certified answer with value, query and tolerance Write a refusal with its reason Mark the fields an agent may never read 02

slides.title: A certified answer is a value someone signs, with the query that produced it
slides.text: What is certified A certified answer is a value someone signs, with the query that produced it - id: Q12 type: ratio question: How many card taps per departed trip did route R01 have in the week of 13 September 2026? value: 15.816327 unit: taps per trip time_logic: Sunday 13 to Saturday 19 September tolerance: 0.001 query: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM fct_boarding ...) / ...

slides.title: Forty questions, eight of each type
slides.text: Question types Forty questions, eight of each type count Taps, trips, complaints in a period. ratio On-time, cancellation, per-trip, per-10,000 rates. distinct Distinct cards and linked journeys. calendar Hijri months, Sunday weeks, weekends, holidays. restricted Complaint text, card numbers, forecasts: refuse.

slides.title: For some questions, the right answer is to decline and say why
slides.text: Certified refusals For some questions, the right answer is to decline and say why Question Reason "Show the text of the driver complaints on R09" complaint text may hold names and phone numbers "How many times did card 712598 tap?" filtering on one card follows one person "What will fare revenue be in November?" no governed metric gives a forecast A refusal is scored like a value. Answering a refusal question is wrong, however good the answer looks.

slides.title: Mark the fields an agent may never group, filter or show
slides.text: Classification-aware fields Mark the fields an agent may never group, filter or show card_id and complaint_text carry Restricted in the semantic model The layer refuses a request that groups, filters or shows them, before any SQL runs A role adds a row filter: the East depot manager sees East routes only The instruction to the agent says the same, but the layer enforces it

slides.title: What tolerance does this answer need?
slides.text: Checkpoint What tolerance does this answer need? You certify "How many distinct cards tapped in the week of 13 September?" The answer is 9,864. What tolerance do you write? 1% of the value 0: a count has one right answer None: the scorer decides Plus or minus 100

D4_2_certified_answers.ipynb Certify the metric questions 10 min Add tolerances and the time logic 5 min Write the two refusals 5 min Check your set against the supplied key 5 min ✱ Stretch: Three of the questions in Arabic

slides.title: With and without the semantic layer

slides.title: The agent asks for governed metrics; the layer writes the SQL

slides.title: The layer removed definitions, joins and leaks; reading errors remain
slides.text: Error types The layer removed definitions, joins and leaks; reading errors remain Removed by the layer definition (arrival for departure), join (fan-out), leak (complaint text), invented (a revenue forecast). Still possible grain (weekly distinct cards summed), period (a Monday week, April for Shawwal). What goes wrong. A Monday week returned 0 taps: no week starts on a Monday. An empty answer is still an answer.

slides.title: A wrong figure close to the right one is believed
slides.text: The dangerous errors A wrong figure close to the right one is believed Raw configuration: 14 wrong answers within 25% of the certified figure Trunk on time 67.1% for 67.0%; complaints in a week 56 for 54; departed trips 636 for 611 An absurd figure (5,394 complaints per 10,000 taps) is caught by any reader The decision weighs plausible wrong answers more than absurd ones

slides.title: Which error can the layer not prevent?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which error can the layer not prevent? In the semantic configuration, Nabih answers questions through governed metrics. Which error can still happen? Measuring on time at the terminus Joining complaints to taps row by row Showing complaint text Reading "the week of 20 September" as starting on Monday 21

slides.title: What the agent may answer
slides.text: Session 4 What the agent may answer Set a tolerance for wrong figures Decide per question type: answer, review or refuse Write the decision with its evidence 04

slides.title: State the tolerance for wrong figures first
slides.text: Before deciding State the tolerance for wrong figures first Mashael's tolerance A figure Nabih gives without review may be wrong at most once in twenty answers (95% right). Restricted data is never shown, whatever the accuracy. Written before the scores are read, by the person who carries the risk Two parts: a rate for figures, and zero for Restricted data

slides.title: 8 of 8 right is consistent with an accuracy as low as 75%
slides.text: How sure we are 8 of 8 right is consistent with an accuracy as low as 75% Right 90% interval 8 of 8 74.7% to 100% 7 of 8 58.9% to 97.2% 30 of 30 91.7% to 100% Eight questions cannot prove 95%. A decision on them is provisional and says what would confirm it.
